transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see us today?

I’ve been thinking about death a lot lately and wondering if my family would be better off without me. My daughter got really worried when I mentioned this to her while we were planning a trip to the Smoky Mountains, so she brought me here to get some help.
Have you experienced any significant changes in your mood or emotional state over the past few weeks or months that might have led to these thoughts about death and your family?

Yes, I've been having these really sharp mood swings for about a year now, especially since I started cutting back my work hours. I sink into these heavy, flat depressions where I feel completely useless and dwell on death, but then a few weeks ago I had a stretch where I felt totally wound-up, wired, and oddly upbeat. It feels like I'm constantly swinging back and forth between those two extremes.

Can you tell me more about the 'wound-up' and 'oddly upbeat' periods, such as how long they lasted and whether you experienced any increased energy, reduced need for sleep, or impulsive behaviors during those times?

Those wound-up spells have been happening on and off for about a year, usually lasting a few weeks, where I'd have so much energy I couldn't sit still and would wake up before dawn to clean and organize. My thoughts would race so fast that it was almost impossible to shut my brain off to sleep. I even almost threw a large chunk of our savings into an online eco-housing project before my daughter stepped in and talked me down.

During those periods when you felt wound-up and oddly upbeat, did you notice any significant impairment in your social or occupational functioning, or were you still able to manage your daily life and relationships without major issues?

During those "up" periods, I felt like I could handle anything and took on way too many commitments with volunteer projects, even almost making a huge mistake with our savings before my daughter stopped me. However, the severe daily impairment—where I completely stopped working, withdrew from friends, and couldn't do household chores—mostly happens when I sink into those heavy, dark depressions.
Did you ever require hospitalization or experience psychotic symptoms, such as hallucinations or delusions, during those wound-up and oddly upbeat periods?
No, I have never been hospitalized during those wound-up times. I also haven't experienced anything like hearing or seeing things that aren't actually there.
Can you estimate how many days or weeks you typically spend in each of these mood states, and do you usually have a period of normal mood in between the depressed and wound-up phases?

I'm not quite sure about the exact number of weeks for each phase, or if there is ever a truly normal period in between. The down, heavy periods seem to last much longer, like this current depression that has been hanging over me steadily for about a year. The wound-up phases feel a lot shorter and are much harder for me to track.
Can you try to estimate or recall roughly how many times you've had these wound-up episodes over the past year, and whether they seem to be getting closer together or staying about the same?

These swings between being wound-up and depressed have been coming and going for at least a year now. I don't have an exact count of how many times it has happened, but they definitely feel like they are ramping up and getting more intense since I started cutting back my work hours.

Can you clarify if the periods of feeling wound-up and the periods of depression occur in a clear, alternating pattern, or if they can occur independently of each other, and have you noticed any specific triggers that seem to switch you from one state to the other?

These high and low states have just been coming and going, swinging back and forth over the past year. The main starting point that really ramped these swings up was discussing and cutting back my work hours for retirement. Other than that, I haven't noticed any specific day-to-day triggers that suddenly switch me from one state to the other.
Can you try to distinguish whether the periods of feeling wound-up are typically followed by a crash into depression, or if they can end without immediately transitioning into a depressive episode?

Yes, it definitely feels like a direct cycle where those wound-up, high-energy stretches are followed by a crash right back into the dark, heavy depression. They have been coming and going like that over the past year, where I sink down almost as soon as the high energy fades.
Can you describe the typical duration of the transition period between the high, wound-up phase and the crash into depression, and whether this transition has been consistent over the past year?

I'm not really sure about the exact duration of the transition period itself, or if it has been consistent each time. All I know is that these swings between feeling wound-up and sinking into depression have been coming and going for at least a year now.
Can you confirm whether the depressive episodes typically last longer than the manic or hypomanic episodes, and if there's a noticeable pattern to the sequence of these episodes over the past year?

Yes, the dark, heavy depressive periods definitely last much longer than the wound-up ones. This hopeless feeling has been hanging over me pretty steadily for about a year, whereas the high-energy spells only last for shorter stretches of a few weeks. I've just been swinging back and forth between those two states over the past year.

Can you clarify if the periods of depression and the periods of feeling wound-up have been occurring in a pattern where the depressive episodes are significantly longer, and if so, have you noticed any periods of relatively normal mood in between these episodes over the past year?

Yes, the heavy depression is definitely much longer and has felt almost constant over the past year, while the wound-up periods are just shorter, intense spells. I really don't feel like I've had any periods of a truly normal or stable mood in between. It seems like I'm always either swinging between those two extremes or just feeling completely weighed down by the depression.
Can you estimate the total number of days in the past year that you've spent in a depressive state versus a wound-up state, to help clarify the pattern and duration of these episodes?

It is really hard for me to give you an exact count of days, but this heavy, depressed feeling has been hanging over me pretty steadily for almost the entire past year. The wound-up, wired periods are much shorter, just happening in temporary stretches of a few weeks at a time within that same year.

Can you confirm if the depressive episodes have consistently lasted at least two weeks, and if the hypomanic episodes have lasted at least four consecutive days, to help differentiate between the diagnostic possibilities?

Yes, the dark, heavy periods definitely last much longer than two weeks, as this current depression has been hanging over me steadily for about a year. And the wound-up, high-energy times also last for several consecutive days at a time, like that stretch a few weeks ago where I was up before dawn cleaning and planning for days on end.
Can you confirm if the wound-up periods have ever lasted less than four consecutive days, or have they consistently met or exceeded that duration?

I'm not entirely sure about the exact number of days those wound-up periods last, as I haven't tracked them precisely. I just know they seem to go on for a stretch of time before I crash back into the heavy depression.
Can you think of any instance where you felt wound-up and your energy was increased, but this period lasted less than four days, to help clarify the nature of these episodes?

I definitely remember having those wound-up, high-energy times, like a few weeks ago when I was constantly cleaning and planning projects. But I'm really not sure of the exact number of days they lasted, or if any of those periods were shorter than four days.
Can you recall any specific instance where a wound-up period lasted only one to three days, to help distinguish between different possible conditions?
I'm really not sure about the exact number of days those wound-up periods lasted. I haven't tracked them closely enough to know if they were ever as short as one to three days.
Can you try to remember if there was ever a time when you felt wound-up and had increased energy, but this feeling only lasted for one to three days, and if so, how you felt after it ended?

I'm not sure about a specific time when those wound-up feelings lasted only one to three days, because my high-energy spells usually felt like they lasted longer or just blurred together. I don't really recall exactly how I felt the moment they ended, other than eventually sinking back into that heavy depression.

Can you think back to any instance where you had a wound-up period that was notably shorter, perhaps only a couple of days, before transitioning back into a depressive state, and if so, did anything distinguish those shorter periods from the longer ones?

I honestly can't recall any specific wound-up periods that lasted only a couple of days. To me, those times all just tend to blur together, so I'm really not sure if there were any shorter ones or how they would have been different.

Can you try to recall if there was ever a time when you felt wound-up and your energy was increased for only a day or two, and if so, did it feel like a full, intense episode or more like a brief, fleeting feeling?
I'm not really sure, and I don't recall those feelings ever being that short. When those wound-up periods happened, they usually seemed to last much longer than just a day or two.

Can you try to remember if you've ever had a period where you felt wound-up and had increased energy, but it only lasted for a very short time, such as just a day, before you felt yourself crashing back into a depressive state?
I'm not really sure, but I don't think they were ever quite that short. I can't recall those wound-up periods lasting for just a single day before I crashed back into the depression.
Can you definitively say that all your wound-up periods have lasted at least four consecutive days, or is it possible that some of them might have been shorter, even if you can't specifically recall?

I'm not entirely sure about the exact number of days or if some of those periods were shorter, as I didn't track the calendar closely during those times. I just recall them as distinct stretches of time where I felt highly energized.
Can you confirm whether all of your wound-up periods have consistently lasted at least four consecutive days, which is a key factor in distinguishing between different conditions?

I'm not entirely sure of the exact number of days those high periods lasted because I never tracked the specific day count. I just know they felt like distinct, intense stretches of time, but I can't say for sure if they always lasted at least four days.
Can you look back over the past year and try to estimate if most of your wound-up periods have lasted at least four consecutive days, even if you can't recall every single episode precisely?

I'm not entirely sure of the exact number of days those wound-up periods lasted, as I didn't keep close track of the time. However, they definitely felt like they lasted for several days at a time when they happened.
Can you make an educated guess about whether most of your wound-up periods over the past year have typically lasted at least four consecutive days, or if some of them might have been shorter?

I'm really not completely sure about the exact number of days those wound-up periods lasted. They definitely felt like they went on for several days at a time, but I just didn't keep close track of the calendar back then.
Can you try to think of any wound-up period that you are certain lasted at least four consecutive days, to help clarify the nature of these episodes?
I'm not entirely sure of the exact number of consecutive days those wound-up periods lasted. They definitely felt like they went on for a stretch, but I just can't pin down the exact number of days.

Can you think of any specific instance where a wound-up period clearly lasted at least four consecutive days, and if so, can you describe how that period differed from any potentially shorter episodes?

I'm not completely sure about the exact number of days or how to compare different episodes. Those wound-up, high-energy periods, like the one a few weeks ago where I was up early cleaning and reorganizing, definitely seemed to last for several days in a row. However, I didn't keep a close track of the calendar, so I can't really compare them to any shorter spells.

Can you think of any specific instance where you had a wound-up period that you are absolutely certain lasted at least four consecutive days, and if so, did it end with a noticeable crash into a depressive state?

Yes, that stretch I had a few weeks ago definitely lasted for about a couple of weeks, which is well over four days. After that high energy finally wore off, I crashed right back down into this heavy, dark depression. It definitely feels like these swings always end with me sinking back down into that dark place.
Can you confirm whether the majority of your wound-up periods have lasted at least four consecutive days, which could help distinguish between different conditions?

I'm still not entirely sure of the exact number of days for most of those periods because I didn't track them closely enough. They certainly felt like they went on for a while, but I can't say for sure if the majority of them lasted at least four days.
Can you confirm one last time whether you're certain that all your wound-up periods have lasted at least four consecutive days, which is crucial for determining the exact nature of your condition?

I understand why that's important, but I'm just not completely sure if every single one of those wound-up periods lasted exactly four consecutive days or more. The ones I remember clearly, like the stretch a few weeks ago, definitely lasted for at least a week or more at a time, but I can't be absolutely certain about the duration of every single episode.
